X-ENV holds, but the note only repeats the parent's line. It should say that model: inherit (or --model) can pick only Claude models, so no plugin setting changes the model family.
IMP-44 should win under precedence: fake agents reach the stuck and partial paths on demand, which is exactly what the reason says was missing. The note already cites it, but X-DONE ranks below IMP.

IMP-33 and IMP-34 fit at least as well: docs tests now enforce the README measurement tie and the changelog entry. IMP-35 leaves RELEASING.md as prose, and its detail does not say that items name commands.

Under the X-HIST rule the note must cite IMP-52, which handles the actionable single-file part: hygiene moved out while SCHEMA stayed with its readers. A shared constant can also be imported across modules.
IMP-52 (the hygiene module split) does not touch hand-kept option tables. IMP-41 does: test_docs reads fivewhys.OPTIONS and pins its count. Otherwise X-HIST citing IMP-41.
Treating the tree as the final product is a design choice, not outside the plugin's control. R-17 (no telemetry, no backend) fits. The note describes the parent (runs are local), not this reason.
The note describes the parent (small additions). A missing baseline is past process: X-HIST citing IMP-52, or X-FALSE because git history keeps the v0.1.0 file and its line count.

R-13 covers scheduled CI evals, but the note is wrong that RELEASING.md reruns the eval every release. It runs only for evals/ changes, and gates go stale only on commits, so drift with no commits is still unchecked. The rest is X-ENV.

JSON nesting is a current design choice, not past history. IMP-32 fits at least as well because its measured 38 tokens per reason include the overhead. The X-HIST rule also requires citing IMP-32 by code, not round-1 R-08.
